citation.title: Application of the hierarchical bootstrap to multi-level data in neuroscience
citation.authors: Varun Saravanan; Gordon J. Berman; Samuel J. Sober

topic: Hierarchical (cluster) bootstrap for nested, non-independent data; neuroscience examples. Not about plasma, CES, or nowcasting.
own_question: Does sequential resampling over hierarchy levels control Type-I error and retain power, compared with pooled, summarized, and LMM analyses?
actual_method_and_evidence: Poisson-firing simulations with subject-level Gaussian offsets. Pooled t-tests showed inflated false positives (about 46% to 96%). The hierarchical bootstrap stayed near 5% for clustered data but was conservative for independent data. It had more power than summarizing in small-N settings. Real reanalyses used songbird and fly datasets. Its pboot is described by the authors as a direct hypothesis probability; that is the authors' interpretation, not established fact.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: When samples are nested within clusters (e.g., many frames per shot), treating them as independent can understate uncertainty. Shot-level (cluster) resampling is one way to account for this.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: pp.5-7, Sec. 2.5 Eq. 2 (design effect); Sec. 3.1.1, Fig. 2
claim_checks.qualification: The evidence comes from neuroscience simulations, not plasma data. Applying shot-level resampling to our uncertainty estimates would be our own methodological choice.

validation_if_relevant: Simulation false-positive and power curves only. There are no temporal holdouts.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite as evidence on CES/BES/ECEI or nowcast accuracy.
Do not present pboot as a validated posterior probability.
Do not claim the bootstrap is unbiased in all cases; it was conservative for independent data.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional methods citation, usable only if we report shot-clustered bootstrap intervals. It is irrelevant to the introduction's physics framing.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
